title: Cross-Function Reentrancy Allowing Drainage of the Reward Vault
value_at_risk: Shared reward vault (ETH) funding all delegator and validator rewards
exploit_path:
1. Deploy a contract, register it as a delegator and stake the minimum weight; wait out the minimum staking duration.
2. Call claimDelegatorRewards(); _reward() sends ETH to the attacker before lastRewardClaimTime/lastClaimUptimeSeconds are written.
3. In receive(), re-enter initiateDelegatorRemoval(); the removal path recalculates rewards from the still-stale timestamps and stores them in _redeemableDelegatorRewards.
4. Call completeDelegatorRemoval() to be paid the stored rewards a second time for the same window.
5. Amplify with many delegator positions (the report describes this) to drain the shared reward vault.
preconditions: Delegator registration available to the attacker (the report PoC registers an attacker contract); minimum stake and staking duration; reward vault funded
notes: ~200% of intended rewards per period per position; the validator path duplicates too when there are no delegation fees. PoC in report. Check registration cost vs reward size for economics.

title: Possibility to use fraudulent Raydium pool to stake worthless LP Tokens and receive staking rewards for legitimate token
entry_point: stake instruction (programs/watt/src/instructions/stake.rs), RaydiumCPMMAccounts in remaining accounts
value_at_risk: Staking reward emissions for legitimate pairs (e.g. WattBONK/USDC)
exploit_path:
1. Create a worthless token (SCAM), wrap it to WattSCAM, create a WattSCAM/USDC Raydium CPMM pool and become the sole LP.
2. Call stake() with the legitimate WattBONK stake-context accounts but pass the WattSCAM/USDC pool accounts in the RaydiumCPMMAccounts remaining accounts.
3. The program never checks that the staked LP mint belongs to the pool implied by watt_mint, so user.liquidity for WattBONK increases.
4. Collect staking rewards for the legitimate pair while the staked LP is worthless.
5. Repeat with fresh pools; rewards are paid out of the shared emission pool.
preconditions: Attacker can create a Raydium CPMM pool permissionlessly; staking emissions active; no capital beyond a dust USDC side
notes: Fixed by validating watt_mint against the LP pool. Report gives a full exploit scenario. Profit is emission dilution of honest stakers; value depends on emission rate.

title: Attacker can steal all funds by repaying already repaid loans
value_at_risk: All lending-pool funds and NFT collateral held by the protocol
exploit_path:
1. Take a loan against an NFT and repay it normally (loan now has borrowedAmount == 0 but still resolves).
2. Take a new loan.
3. Call repay() with the OLD loan id; repayAmount is capped to borrowedAmount = 0, the loan is marked repaid and the NFT collateral for the old loan is returned again (BeraBond version needs a 1 wei msg.value to pass the zero-amount check).
4. Repeat steps 2-3: each cycle extracts an NFT for free / re-withdraws collateral while the protocol's funds back the new loan.
5. Iterate until the pool is drained.
preconditions: Attacker has one NFT to seed the cycle; lending pool funded; repay() accepts already-repaid loan ids
notes: Fixed in ceac8609. The mechanism as written returns the same NFT twice; the profit is bounded by how much the protocol will lend against the re-used collateral. Verify the loan-id lifecycle (is the old id still resolvable after repay?).

title: The redeemShort function is available before the pool is closed
value_at_risk: Pool collateral / payoutToken reserves backing short positions
exploit_path:
1. Hold short-token shares in a pool that has not yet closed.
2. Call redeemShort() before the pool closes, when balanceChangePerShare is still 0.
3. payout = (cap - 0) * collateralMinted / relativeAmount, i.e. the maximum possible payout, and the caller's short shares are burned.
4. The caller receives the maximum payout early; the pool is left under-collateralised for the eventual close and for other short holders.
preconditions: Pool not yet closed; attacker holds short shares; payoutToken liquidity in the pool
notes: Fixed in 0781fb97. The report states the payout is maximal at balanceChangePerShare == 0. Stage 2 should confirm the short shares can be acquired cheaply before close (otherwise the attacker pays fair value for the max payout).

title: Multiple Account Ownership Validation Vulnerabilities Across Pool Creation, Contribution, and Staking Systems Enable Fee Diversion and Unauthorized Access
value_at_risk: Launchpad pool allocations (free tokens) and staking-tier benefits; platform fee revenue
exploit_path:
1. contribute_usd1: pass your own token account as pool_usd1_vault and treasury_usd1_account; the program only checks the mint, not ownership, so the 'contribution' never reaches the pool but the contribution is recorded.
2. stake_usd1: pass your own account as usd1_staking_vault, so stake_usd1 records a stake without transferring tokens, granting higher allocation tiers.
3. Claim the pool allocation funded by honest contributors.
4. Optionally create pools with your own treasury accounts so fees return to you.
preconditions: Pool live with honest contributions; attacker can create token accounts with the expected mint
notes: Multiple independent ownership-check omissions; the free-allocation path is the profitable one. Solved by the client, so Stage 2 should check the deployed program id for the constraint fix.

title: C01. Investors funds can be drained using FrictionlessTransferManager
value_at_risk: All ERC-20 tokens that investors have approved to the TransferManager
exploit_path:
1. Deploy a malicious ERC-3643 token and register yourself as its agent (the attacker controls the token's compliance rules).
2. Create/accept a transfer offer where the malicious token is one side and a victim's approved token is the other.
3. confirmTransferOffer() only checks that msg.sender is an agent for one of the traded tokens; with the attacker as agent of their own token, the check passes.
4. The manager pulls the victim's tokens (previously approved to it) as the counterparty leg and delivers them to the attacker.
5. Repeat for every approved holder.
preconditions: Victims have outstanding approvals to FrictionlessTransferManager; attacker can deploy an ERC-3643 token and self-register as agent
notes: Classic 'authorization checks the wrong token' bug. Profit equals the aggregate outstanding allowance, which for a transfer manager is typically large. Confirm agent self-registration is permissionless in the deployed token factory.

title: Unstake function allows full withdrawal while maintaining staking position
value_at_risk: Staking reward emissions and the staked LP pool
exploit_path:
1. Stake 1000 LP tokens; user_stake_state.lp_token_amount = 1000.
2. Call unstake(amount = 1). The instruction transfers the FULL staked amount (1000 LP) from the vault to the user but only decrements the recorded stake by 1.
3. The attacker now holds the LP tokens back and still has 999 LP recorded as staked.
4. Keep claiming rewards on the phantom stake, and repeat the partial unstake until the recorded position is drained of real backing.
preconditions: Staking live; attacker has staked LP
notes: Report marks it fixed. The bug pays out the full balance on a partial unstake - direct double-dip of principal plus rewards. Distinct from the fake-pool finding (C7) in the same program.

title: Using Uniswap spot price is subject to manipulation
entry_point: Uniswap V3 quoter used for withdrawal, borrow, repay and liquidation valuation
value_at_risk: Margin-trading pool liquidity and other users' collateral
exploit_path:
1. Flash-borrow and swap to move the Uniswap V3 pool price of the collateral token (report PoC doubles WETH from 4,000 to 8,000 USDC).
2. Deposit 1 WETH and borrow against the manipulated quote - the PoC borrows 7,000 USDC against 1 WETH.
3. Unwind the swap, leaving the position under-collateralised by the manipulation profit.
4. Default / let liquidation fail to recover; the shortfall is socialised to the pool.
preconditions: Flash liquidity on the pool; quoter read in the same transaction; borrow cap above true collateral value
notes: Report includes a Foundry PoC with a quoter mock that sets the price. Stage 2 must confirm the production quoter reads the live pool (not a mock) and that borrow/liquidation use the same spot quote.
